16.text: in the Koryak conceptions of “guardians” less absolute.

17.text: In consonance with this latter assertion, perhaps, incantations are held in

18.text: hardly less esteem among the Chukchee. Magic formulas must be pronounced

19.text: during their ceremonials, and with them certain prescriptions must be carried

20.text: out. Ignorance of these requirements, or neglect in the performance of them,

21.text: menaces the power of the ceremonial, and may cause a withdrawal of the

22.text: protecting forces and an attack by hostile “spirits.” Most of the younger

23.text: people, of course, on being asked about such formulas, declared that they had

24.text: no knowledge of them, and that they performed only the outward part of

25.text: the ceremonials, according to the example of their forefathers. They ascribe

26.text: this ignorance to their own foolishness and to the tendency of modern times

27.text: to a disbelief in the mysterious, or even to the ridicule of it as mere super-

28.text: stition. In this, however, they are not quite sincere, because, on the whole,

29.text: it is considered advisable to conceal everything about the incantations. Usually

30.text: one of the older members of the family will know at least a few of them,

31.text: which he will use to make his ceremonials more effective. It is true that

32.text: some of the more careless people do actually perform their ceremonials

33.text: without incantations, but this state of things continues only till some misfortune

34.text: befalls them. The latter would at once be imputed to such unprotected state,
